sharedRules.name: Innate Weapons
sharedRules.description:
When Choosing Equipment and Abilities, a model part can only choose Innate Weapons if it has no other options.
--
All model parts with Mount, Beast, Construct come equipped with Innate Weapons as their default equipment and cannot lose them.

sharedRules.name: Hand Weapon
sharedRules.description:
When Choosing Equipment and Abilities, a model part can only choose a Hand Weapon if it has no other options, or is a Weapon Master. 
 Models with a Shield using a Hand Weapon gain Parry.
--
All model parts without Innate Weapons come equipped with a Hand Weapon as their default equipment and cannot lose it.

sharedRules.name: Great Weapon
sharedRules.description:
Two-Handed
+2 Str, +2 AP, always Agi

sharedRules.name: Halberd
sharedRules.description:
Two-Handed
+1 Str, +1 AP

sharedRules.name: Lance
sharedRules.description:
Devastating Charge (+2 Str, +2 AP, +1 Agi)
Only models with Mount, Centauroid can use a Lance.

sharedRules.name: Light Lance
sharedRules.description:
Devastating Charge (+1 Str, +1 AP)
Only models with Mount, Centauroid can use a Light Lance.

sharedRules.name: Paired Weapons
sharedRules.description:
Two-Handed. 
Attacks made with Paired Weapons ignore Parry.
+1 Att, +1 Off

sharedRules.name: Spear
sharedRules.description:
Fight in Extra Rank
+1 Agi, +1 AP, and +1 additional AP towards Mount, Centauroid
Models with Mount, Centauroid cannot use a Spear.

sharedRules.name: Fields
sharedRules.description:
Fields can be represented in the game for example by meadows of tall grass, or agricultural enclosures.
 Fields have the following rules: Covering Terrain (Soft Cover, Height 3) for units in contact.# Flammable: units in contact gain 
 Weakness (Flaming Attacks).

sharedRules.name: Forest
sharedRules.description:
Forests can be represented for example by jungles, brushwoods, or small groves of trees. 
 Forests have the following rules: Covering Terrain (Soft Cover, Height 5).# Dangerous Terrain (6+, Mount).# Disruptive Terrain.

sharedRules.name: Hills
sharedRules.description:
Hills can be represented for example by elevated plateaus or burial mounds. 
 Hills have the following rules: Elevated Position: a model is considered to have an Elevated Position if it is fully on a Hill. 
 For the purposes of determining Cover and for drawing Line of Sight to or from a model with Elevated Position, ignore intervening models that do not have an Elevated Position. # Opaque Terrain. Remember that Line of Sight can still be drawn into and out of the Terrain Feature.

sharedRules.name: Impassable Terrain
sharedRules.description:
Impassable Terrain can be represented for example by monoliths, cliffs, massive boulders, or buildings. 
 Impassable Terrain has the following rules: Dangerous Terrain (4+) for units making Flee Moves through it.# Impassable: models cannot move into or through an Impassable Terrain Feature (except as part of a Flee Move).# Opaque Terrain.

sharedRules.name: Ruins
sharedRules.description:
Ruins can be represented for example by rubble, abandoned farmsteads or ancient sites of symbolic or arcane power.
 Ruins have the following rules: Covering Terrain (Hard Cover, Height 3) for units in contact.# Dangerous Terrain (6+).

sharedRules.name: Walls
sharedRules.description:
Walls can be represented for example by stone, wood, or makeshift structures.
 Walls have the following rules: Covering Terrain (Hard Cover, Height 3) for units in contact.# Dangerous Terrain (6+, Construct).# Fortified Position Attack Attribute: Melee Attacks from Charging models that are in contact with a Wall suffer a -1 to hit penalty. 
 This also applies to Supporting Attacks made by Charging models over models in contact with a Wall, and to attacks across gaps where the model’s virtual extended base would be in contact with a Wall.

sharedRules.name: Water Terrain
sharedRules.description:
Water Terrain can be represented in the game for example by ponds, swamps, or rivers.
 Water Terrain has the following rules: Dangerous Terrain (6+, Metal Armour).# Disruptive Terrain.# Soaked: units in contact gain 
 Immune (Flaming Attacks).# Unsure Footing: models in contact cannot use Impact Hits, Stomp Attack.

sharedRules.name: Tales of the Fallen
sharedRules.description: Mooarrgh has the following Spell Scrolls: Danse Macabre (Evocation), Umbral Majesty (Occultism), Wild Guardian (Shamanism), Dragon’s Roar (Pyromancy) If a friendly Character anywhere on the Battlefield is removed as a casualty or removes an enemy Character as a casualty whilst being Engaged in Combat, select one of Mooarrgh used Spell Scrolls: the selected Scroll can be used again.

sharedRules.name: Standing in Wait
sharedRules.description:
During Pre-game Selections, select either : 
 • Attached, Teach by Example 
 • Solitary, Sleeper, and Ambush (Field, Forest, Water Terrain).

sharedRules.name: Teach by Example
sharedRules.description:
Any unit containing Ghaa! benefits from Swiftstride, Stubborn, Mindless. 
In addition, choose a single Minotaurs unit with a maximum of 5 models. The selected unit gains Ambush (Battlefield Edge), and Ghaa! must enter the Battlefield joined to it.

sharedRules.name: Abandon All Hope
sharedRules.description: During Tristitia’s Shooting Phase, they can make a Shooting Attack that targets all enemy units within 12" of Tristitia (including those Engaged in Combat and outside Front Arc and/or Line of Sight). Each target suffers 1 hit for each Rank it has, with Strength 9, Armour Penetration 10, Psychic Attacks, Magical Attacks. This attack can be used even if Tristitia is Engaged in Combat.

sharedRules.name: Growing Despair
sharedRules.description: Afflict (-1 Dis, -X Def, and -X Off), where 'X' is equal to the number of the current Game Turn.

sharedRules.name: Commander of the Steppes
sharedRules.description: At the start of each friendly Player Turn, you may select a friendly unit within 12" of Tergon Khan entirely with Mount. The selected unit gains Extra Support (+1) and Strider. Duration: One Turn.

sharedRules.name: Revoke the Mandate of Heaven
sharedRules.description:
Each Character or model with Dragon that either: 
 • Breaks from a Round of Combat in which a unit containing Tergon Khan was Engaged, or 
 • Selects Flee! as a Charge Reaction when a unit containing Tergon Khan declared a Charge
Suffers D3 hits with Str 6, AP 3, Magical Attacks, Zeal (against Dragon).

sharedRules.name: A Watery Grave
sharedRules.description:
Tethaen is always considered to have rolled a 3+ when rolling for whether he arrives using Ambush. 
In addition, at the beginning of “Post Combat” (Round of Combat, Step 6), if Tethaen won the Round of Combat and an enemy Character in that Combat was removed as a casualty, then Tethaen may be placed in Ambush.

sharedRules.name: Barbed Nets
sharedRules.description: Afflict (-1 Str, -1 AP)

sharedRules.name: Blessed by Harag
sharedRules.description:
Tethaen’s rags and strange hat never stop dripping, even when out of the water.
Aegis (5+),Resistance (against Flaming Attacks).

sharedRules.name: Grim Harpoon
sharedRules.description:
Counts as a Great Weapon in Melee. +1 Att.
Any unit that suffers one or more ranged hits from this weapon loses Swiftstride, and cannot regain it in any way, until the start of the Active Player’s next Turn.

sharedRules.name: Aembeghen’s Blades
sharedRules.description:
Paired Weapons. If there are any enemy Characters in contact with the wielder’s unit, the Black Rose gains +2 Att.
 In addition, any Melee Attacks the Black Rose allocates against a Character gain +2 Str, +4 AP.

sharedRules.name: Dance of the Rose
sharedRules.description:
When Choosing Equipment and Abilities, the Black Rose must choose one of the following Dances, with Duration: Round of Combat. The Black Rose cannot select a specific Dance again until one or more of the following has occurred: 
 • She is not Engaged in Combat. 
 • She has selected all Dances. 
 • She can only select Dance of Caedhren, and it is not possible to do the Make Way. 
 Dances: 
 • Dance of Caedhren: the Black Rose can use Make Way, even if she is already in contact with an enemy model, provided she moves into contact with an enemy Character in her unit’s Front Facing. 
 • Dance of Ceinran: Nominate one enemy Character model in contact with the Black Rose. The Black Rose and the selected Character always have 0 Attacks, and no attacks nor hits can be assigned to either. At Agility Step 0, the Black Rose rolls 1D3, Maximized, and the selected Character rolls 1D3. If either model rolls lower, it loses a number of Health Points equal to the difference between the two rolls. 
 • Dance of Nabh:
 The Black Rose gains Hatred (against Characters),Zeal (against Characters). 
Attacks against the Black Rose gain +1 to hit.

sharedRules.name: The Obsidian Thorns
sharedRules.description:
The Black Rose gains Exclusive (Obsidian Guard), Magic Resistance (1), and all models in her unit gain +1 Charge Speed. 
 In addition, enemy units are not allowed to choose the Flee! Charge Reaction to Charges declared on them by the Black Rose’s unit, unless they are Shaken. 
 Note: this has no influence on Charge Reactions from other units.

sharedRules.name: The Living Law
sharedRules.description: At the beginning of each Friendly Melee Phase, select an enemy unit on your opponent’s Army List. The selected unit becomes marked for the purpose of Ancient Grudge. Duration: Permanent.

sharedRules.name: The High Lore Keeper
sharedRules.description:
Dwarfs know to guard the High Lorekeeper.
The High Lorekeeper counts as a King for fullfilling the requirments of Bodyguard.

sharedRules.name: Wonders of the Age
sharedRules.description:
Duna Bregold’s Paired Weapons have the following Runic Enchantments: Rune of Might, Rune of Anger, Rune of Precision. 
 In addition, Duna Bregold has the following Runic Artefacts: Rune of Denial, Rune of Devouring, Rune of Grounding. This is in addition to the usual limitation of Runic Items, however the Rune of Denial, Rune of Devouring, Rune of Grounding cannot be activated by other friendly models.

sharedRules.name: The Aleward Crew
sharedRules.description: When Tador Berafrig is Deployed, all Rank-and-File models in that unit gains +1 Armour and Aegis (3+, against Flaming Attacks). Duration: Permanent.

sharedRules.name: Master Brewer
sharedRules.description:
During each friendly Magic Phase, at any time before Casting Spells (Magic Phase, 5), the Master Brewer may select a single of the following Ales to affect his unit. Duration: One Turn. 
 • Stout Ale: Stubborn, Fearless, Unruly. 
 • Bitter Ale: Hatred, Fury, Unruly. 
 • Red Ale: Zeal, Lethal Strike, Unruly.

sharedRules.name: A Koelhund’s Chase
sharedRules.description: Rolls for Charge Range and Pursue Distance by the model’s unit gain Maximized.

sharedRules.name: Divine Jurisdiction
sharedRules.description:
All Inquisitors may give the Steady, Men! Order to their units. 
In addition, an Army List containing Heinrich Falkenbach changes the following Orders: 
 • Brace For Impact! changes into: Cut the Head of the Snake!: 
 - The target gains Fury (against units containing a Character), First Strike (Hatred (against Character)). 
 • Ready! Aim! Fire! changes into Aim for the Weak Spot! 
 - If an attack with Aim for the Weak Spot! wounds with a to-wound roll of ‘6’, neither Aegis nor Regeneration Saves can be taken against it.

sharedRules.name: Gregor’s Holy Hammer
sharedRules.description:
Hand Weapon, +1 Str, +1 AP, Multiple Wounds (2, against Aegis or Regeneration*). 
 *Including against models with Aegis or Regeneration Saves with conditional applications.

sharedRules.name: Fanatical Devotion
sharedRules.description: Models in Brother Tomaz's unit benefit from Regeneration (6+), and model parts without Mount benefit from Hatred.

sharedRules.name: Officially Not A Miracle
sharedRules.description: The Rank-and-File Health Pool Brother Tomaz is joined to Raises 1 HP at the start of each friendly Magic Phase.

sharedRules.name: Repent!
sharedRules.description: +1 Att, Crush Attack.

sharedRules.name: Shepherding the Flock
sharedRules.description:
Brother Tomaz can join Flagellants as if he was Unstable.
As long as he is joined to Flagellants, he is Unstable.

sharedRules.name: Commander of the Veil
sharedRules.description:
Arcanadh is equipped with the following Magic Items:
Obsidian Rock, Potion of Power Preservation, Scroll of Power.
These Magic Items cannot be taken by other friendly models.

sharedRules.name: Shroud Seekers
sharedRules.description: All friendly units gain +1 Defensive Skill and +1 Offensive Skill when in contact with an enemy unit containing a Magic Item.

sharedRules.name: Rogue Heroine
sharedRules.description: The model gains Fearless, Frenzy, and is unaffected by Beacon of Courage.

sharedRules.name: Scourge of Fleets
sharedRules.description: Balûruth gains Grind Attack (D6, Str 4, AP 1, Flaming Attacks).

sharedRules.name: Meeting of Minds
sharedRules.description: The model gains Resistance (Flaming Attacks).

sharedRules.name: The Lance of Tears
sharedRules.description:
Lance. The model gains Afflict (-1 Dis), Dhaenala gains +1 Att and Fury, Hatred. 
 In addition, she loses 1 Attack at the end of every Game Turn in which she was NOT Engaged in Combat. Duration: Permanent.

sharedRules.name: The Riddle of Peace
sharedRules.description:
During Pre-game Selections, select a single Character on the opponent’s Army List. 
Any unit containing the selected Character suffers from Minimised (Charge Range Roll).

sharedRules.name: Blivet Lance
sharedRules.description: Lance. Devastating Charge (+5 Agi). Attacks with the Blivet Lance ignore negative modifiers to to-hit rolls.

sharedRules.name: Burning Armour
sharedRules.description: Each time a Standard Melee Attack allocated against Ibat-Sokavum results in a to-hit roll of ‘1’, the attacking model’s Health Pool suffers a hit with Str 4, AP 0, Flaming Attacks, Automatic Hits.

sharedRules.name: Helm of Kadim Command
sharedRules.description: Model parts with Kadim in friendly units within 12" of Ibat-Sokavum gain First Strike (Hatred (against Weakness (Flaming Attacks))).

sharedRules.name: Fae Breasplate
sharedRules.description: +1 Arm and Distracting (1).

sharedRules.name: A Worthy Foe
sharedRules.description: Knightly Principle. During Pre-game Selections, choose a single enemy Character or a single Height 4-5 enemy model with Solitary: King Henry gains Multiple Wounds (10, against the chosen model).

sharedRules.name: Feyforged Lance
sharedRules.description: Lance. Devastating Charge (+2 Att), Lethal Strike, Zeal

sharedRules.name: Our Brave King
sharedRules.description:
Combats containing a friendly unit where the Rank-and-File models contains Commonfolk within 12" of King Henry the Young gain a bonus to Static Combat Resolution equal to the number of unsaved wounds inflicted by King Henry the Young in the current Melee Phase.
This does not apply to Combats King Henry is a part of.

sharedRules.name: New Guard
sharedRules.description:
Dukes cannot be taken in an Army List containing King Henry the Young.
In addition, friendly units containing a Folk Hero with Castellan benefit from +1 Mob.

sharedRules.name: “Borrowed” Steed
sharedRules.description: Immediately before choosing a unit to join using the Hidden rule, Hernaut may gain a “Destrier” mount for free, without any upgrades.

sharedRules.name: Infuriating Wit
sharedRules.description: Maximised (Charge Range rolls) towards any unit containing Hernaut.

sharedRules.name: Taunt
sharedRules.description: Units declaring a charge towards a unit containing Hernaut gain Maximised (Charge Range rolls) with the Duration: One Phase.

sharedRules.name: Leprechaun Companion
sharedRules.description: Each Standard Melee Attack allocated against Hernaut that fails its to-hit roll is instead allocated towards the attacking model’s Health Pool with Automatic Hits.

sharedRules.name: Been There, Done That.
sharedRules.description: Every friendly unit of Mercenary Veterans and Mercenary Gunners gains Bodyguard (Ganzorig). In addition, when joined to one of these units, Ganzorig benefits from any Extraordinary Model Rule upgrades the unit has.

sharedRules.name: Get the Job Done!
sharedRules.description: One use only. During 'Calculate Final Combat Score' (Round of Combat, step 4.B), Ganzorig may Recover up to 2 Health Points and adds +2 Combat Resolution to his side.

sharedRules.name: The Ironbond
sharedRules.description: The model gains Resistance, Stubborn.

sharedRules.name: Young Mercenaries
sharedRules.description: All friendly Bruiser model parts in an army containing Ganzorig benefit from First Strike (Fury), as long as he is on the Battlefield.

sharedRules.name: Eru’s Secret Recipes
sharedRules.description:
At the start of each friendly Player Turn, pick one of the following to affect the Chefling’s unit. Duration: One Turn. 
 • Bluehoove Goat Stew: +2 Mob, Strider 
 • Trollbear Goulash: Regeneration (6+), Recover a single HP on a Rank-and-File model in the Chefling’s unit.
 • Stonecold Soup: Disciplined, Courageous, Channel (1)

sharedRules.name: Ghost Pepper
sharedRules.description: During each friendly Shooting Phase, select a single model part in the Chefling’s unit: it gains Breath Attack (Str 3, AP 0). Duration: One Phase.

sharedRules.name: Gone but not Forgotten
sharedRules.description:
If Valish is removed as a casualty, all friendly model parts with Ogre gain Hatred (against the unit that caused Valish to be removed as a casualty*). Duration: Permanent. 
 * This includes all models joined to it.

sharedRules.name: Higher Standards
sharedRules.description: Rank and File units containing Troll in an Army List containing Lerrgog are upgraded with a Standard Bearer. Duration: Permanent. This affects Battle Preparations.

sharedRules.name: Ironmaul Limb
sharedRules.description: Each time Troll Toll’s effect is triggered, Lerrgog performs two Standard Melee Attacks instead of a single one.

sharedRules.name: Troll’s Bellow
sharedRules.description: When you activate the War Cry!, all friendly model parts with Troll gain Fury. Duration: One Turn.

sharedRules.name: Born in Fire
sharedRules.description: When Choosing Equipment and Abilities, Mokrog may gain Flaming Attacks. Duration: Round of Combat.

sharedRules.name: Destined to Conquer
sharedRules.description: The model gains Fearless.

sharedRules.name: The bigger the Axe…
sharedRules.description: Great Weapon. When Choosing Equipment and Abilities, Mokrog may choose to gain either Multiple Wounds (2), Hatred. Duration: Round of Combat.

sharedRules.name: The Only King
sharedRules.description:
All models in the Only King’s unit benefit from Dying Blow. 
 In addition, if The Only King is removed as a casualty, all friendly units lose Brood Rivalry. This effect persists for the Duration of One Turn after Mokrog is removed as a casualty. This is an exception to the rule 4.C of the “Attacks” chapter: “Losing the Last Health Point”.

sharedRules.name: Chosen Warlord
sharedRules.description: Mokrog counts as an Orc Warlord for the purpose of War Cry!

sharedRules.name: 'Tis but a scratch
sharedRules.description: Mokrog gains Aegis (5+).

sharedRules.name: Still Kickin'
sharedRules.description:
At the beginning of any Player Turn after the Splendid Leader has been removed as a casualty, you can Summon a new Splendid Leader using the Hidden rule, with the following exceptions: you can select whether the new Splendid Leader will be mounted on a Beastie, the Splendid Palanquin or a Beastie Chariot before choosing the unit he appears in.
If the Splendid Palanquin is selected, ignore the Base Size limitation and select six Rank-and-File models in the unit to be joined instead of a single model. After choosing an eligible unit, remove the six Rank-and-File models so that the Splendid Leader is placed in the Front Rank, where the removed models were positioned.

sharedRules.name: Brilliant Agitator
sharedRules.description: The Splendid Leader counts as a Goblin Demagogue for the purpose of War Cry!

sharedRules.name: Eternity Chamber
sharedRules.description: This device is said to have protected her for ages and it bestows upon her powerful protective abilities. Its effects are included in her profile.

sharedRules.name: Greater Guiding Mastery
sharedRules.description: Friendly models containing Magnasaur in units within 12" of Anurarch Destined benefit from Pack Hunter.

sharedRules.name: Like the Tyrants of Old
sharedRules.description:
Anurarch Destined is both General and Battle Standard Bearer. 
 In addition, an Army List containing Anurarch Destined cannot include any other Character, neither the Monolith of Vitalism nor a Koru Stone.

sharedRules.name: Utterly Ruthless
sharedRules.description: The first time each turn Anurarch Destined performs The Sacrifice and inflicts Health Point losses with it, she Recovers 1 HP.

sharedRules.name: Balance of Nature
sharedRules.description: Wizard Conclave (3). Instead of the usual Spell Selection (including Spell Swapping), Shade and Stone must select one spell from Druidism Apprentice and Adept spells, one spell from Shamanism Apprentice and Adept spells, and must always select the Hereditary Spell.

sharedRules.name: Harmony of the Sun
sharedRules.description: All other friendly models in units within 8" of Shade and Stone benefit from Regeneration (+1, max. 4+).

sharedRules.name: Violence of the Storm
sharedRules.description: The Conjuring Shade model part is always considered affected by Awaken the Beast (Shamanism).

sharedRules.name: The World Tree
sharedRules.description:
Ancient Dawael does not select his spells during list building, instead during Pre-game Selections, Ancient Dawael must select one of the following model rules with duration: Permanent. He also knows the associated forth spell. 
 • Colony of Frogs 
 • Murder of Crows 
 • Nest of Vipers

sharedRules.name: Thickened Brush
sharedRules.description: One use only. Can be activated at the beginning of the enemy's turn. For each friendly unit within 12" and entirely with Sylvan Spirit, any enemy unit in contact with it loses Devastating Charge. Duration: One Turn.

sharedRules.name: Colony of Frogs
sharedRules.description:
Add the following Offensive Model Part to Ancient Dawael:
AttOffStrAPAgiFrog (6)12204Toxic Attacks.
Ancient Dawael gains Strider (Water Terrain).
 One use only. Duration: One Turn. May be activated at the start of any Player Turn. Friendly units entirely with Sylvan Spirit within 12" of Ancient Dawael gain Immune (Flaming Attacks).

sharedRules.name: Murder of Crows
sharedRules.description:
Add the following Offensive Model Part to Ancient Dawael:
AttOffStrAPAgiCrow (6)12204Afflict (-1 Combat Resolution).
Ancient Dawael gains Hatred (against Flying) and Afflict (-1 Def).
 One use only. Duration: One Turn. May be activated at the start of any Player Turn. Choose an enemy unit within 24" of Ancient Dawael. All models with Fly in the chosen unit halve their Charge Range and Mobility, rounding fractions up.

sharedRules.name: Nest of Vipers
sharedRules.description:
Add the following Offensive Model Part to Ancient Dawael:
AttOffStrAPAgiViper (6)12204Poison Attacks.
Ancient Dawael gains Immune (Poison Attacks).
 One use only. Duration: One Turn. May be activated at the start of any Player Turn. Friendly units entirely with Sylvan Spirit within 12" of Ancient Dawael gain: Enemy units in contact with this unit lose Devastating Charge.

sharedRules.name: The Unicorn’s Fury
sharedRules.description: Hand Weapon. Divine Attacks, Devastating Charge (+1 Str, +1 AP, and +X Att, where “X” is equal to the number of Ranks in a single enemy unit in contact, up to a maximum of 4.)

sharedRules.name: The Unicorn’s Horn
sharedRules.description: Spear. +1 Str, +1 AP

sharedRules.name: The Unicorn’s Path
sharedRules.description: One use only. When initiating or ending a Move Manoeuvre in a friendly Movement Phase, Domethil can change a Water, Ruins, Fields Terrain Feature he is in contact with to a Forest of the same size.

sharedRules.name: Charioteer of the Sun
sharedRules.description: During 'Check Combat Formations' (Round of Combat, 2.A), the Rehnepeh model part gains a bonus to its Att, Off, Str, AP, and Agi equal to half the number of Rank-and-File Skeleton Chariot models in his unit, rounding fractions up.

sharedRules.name: Staff of Pi-Ankh Khahiroth
sharedRules.description: A unit containing the Staff of Pi-Ankh Khahiroth benefits from Ghost Step, Strider. In addition, all attacks made by model parts with Mount benefit from Flaming Attacks, Magical Attacks.

sharedRules.name: The Golden Chariot
sharedRules.description:
Rehnepeh gains Distracting,Beacon of Courage (12"). 
In addition, a unit containing The Golden Chariot can never benefit from Cover.

sharedRules.name: Assailed Sanity
sharedRules.description:
Once per turn, when she fails a Casting Roll for a Learned Spell using three or more Magic Dice, she can reroll the dice. If this reroll contains a double, she suffers a Miscast (equal to the Casting Roll as normal).
Note that this applies even if the spell fails or is Dispelled, and that she only suffers a single Miscast per casting.

sharedRules.name: The Lost and Damned
sharedRules.description:
In an Army List containing Ashotet, Skeleton Warriors and Skeleton Cavalry gain Tormented Souls.
In addition, neither of the following unit entries may be included: Death Cult Hierarch, Casket of Phatep, Rehnepeh the Undying Sun, nor any model with Undying Will.

sharedRules.name: The Pyramidion
sharedRules.description:
Spells cast by Ashotet gain +6" Range.
In addition, Ashotet can cast a unique Bound Spell (6+): 
 Surge of Mad Spirits: Range : 24"; Type : Hex, Damage; Duration : Instant.
 The target must take a Courage Test rolling an additional D6. If failed, it suffers a number of hits equal to the amount by which the test was failed. Those hits wound automatically and have Armour Penetration 10.",

sharedRules.name: Tormented Souls
sharedRules.description:
The model gains Aegis (5+, against non-Magical Attacks), Exclusive (Tormented Souls), Ghost Step, Horror, Unruly and Spirit. The model’s Armour is set to 0, it loses Shield, and Skeleton and its Resurrected value is halved. 
All model parts gain +1 AP, Hatred, Magical Attacks, lose all their Weapons, and gain Innate Weapons.

sharedRules.name: Dance of Death
sharedRules.description:
For every Health Point Lady Chrysélie inflicts with a Standard Melee Attack: 
 • Immediately roll another Standard Melee Attack allocated at the same Health Pool as the initial attack. 
 • Resolve these attacks before removing any casualties. 
 • These new attacks do not generate any further attacks.

sharedRules.name: Thirsty Rapiers
sharedRules.description: Paired Weapons. Lethal Strike. For every Health Point loss dealt with this Weapon, immediately roll a D6: on 5+, Lady Chrysélie Recovers a single Health Point. However, all Vampiric rolls she makes automatically fail.

sharedRules.name: Coven of Skulls
sharedRules.description: When the Collective of Varyag casts Arise! (Hereditary Spell), they may choose to set the spell’s Range to 6" and give it the Type: Aura. This choice is declared when choosing targets.

sharedRules.name: Ever Growing
sharedRules.description: Whenever the Collective of Varyag is the target of Arise! (Hereditary Spell), they can Raise Health Points above their number of starting Health Points, to a maximum of twice their starting Health Points.

sharedRules.name: Inergon injection!
sharedRules.description:
One use only. Duration: One Phase. 
 In the Movement Phase, before moving, Professor Mauss can gain Random Movement (3D6").

sharedRules.name: Superior Darkstone Power
sharedRules.description:
Professor Mauss can choose not to move despite having Random Movement.
The model cannot choose to Pursue, unless it is its First Round of Combat and it is Charging. In that case, it must Pursue (including Overrun).

sharedRules.name: Disorienting Scent
sharedRules.description: Afflict (-2 Off), against model parts with Beast, Magnasaur.

sharedRules.name: Mistress of Smoke
sharedRules.description:
One use only. 
When the Shadowslice Stalker would be removed as a casualty or flee while joined to a unit, remove her from the Battlefield: she becomes Hidden again. If she uses this ability and hasn’t been removed as a casualty at the end of the game, the opponent still receives Victory Points as if she had been removed as a casualty.

sharedRules.name: Shadowslice’s Panoply
sharedRules.description:
The Shadowslice Stalker is equipped with the most advanced selection of murderous weaponry known to any species. Each time the Stalker is Deployed using Hidden, she gains one of the following Magic Items. Duration: Permanent. 
 • Countless Daggers: First Strike (+2 Att), Paired Weapons and Throwing Weapons (2+). 
 • Darkstone Rod: +2 Str, Lightning Attacks, Multiple Wounds (2) 
 • Senator’s Toga: +2 Dis, Commanding Presence (6)

sharedRules.name: Escape Routes
sharedRules.description:
One use only. 
At the beginning of any player turn after The Shadowslice Stalker has been removed as a casualty you can Summon a new The Shadowslice Stalker using her Hidden rule.

sharedRules.name: Memory of a Hoarded Blade
sharedRules.description: If included in an Army List not containing Favour of Greed, Joulgrim gains +2 Str, +2 AP and always strikes at Agility Step 0.

sharedRules.name: The Father’s Gifts
sharedRules.description:
At the beginning of each friendly Player Turn, Joulgrim can choose a single friendly unit within 12" to gain one of the following abilities, with Duration: One Turn. 
 • Supernal Shield: the chosen unit suffers -3 Arm and gains Aegis (5+). 
 • Unholy Edge: the chosen unit always strikes at Agility Step 0 and gains +1 AP. 
 • The Eight-Point Crown: the chosen unit suffers -1 Str and -1 AP, and gains Unstable, Stubborn.

sharedRules.name: Protean Limbs
sharedRules.description: please stop blocking the book

sharedRules.name: Duplicate Model Rules
sharedRules.description:
Most Model Rules are not cumulative. This means that if a model or a model part gains the same rule multiple times, the effects do not stack or provide extra benefits. 
This includes Model Rules with different keywords attached (such as Multiple Wounds (towards Height 2) and Multiple Wounds (towards Height 3)), which are considered to be the same Model Rule, meaning that both instances cannot be applied simultaneously. 
 In such cases, the owner may choose which instance of the Model Rule to use at any time.

sharedRules.name: Model Rules and Units
sharedRules.description:
Even though Model Rules are given to individual models, some of them function on a unit level, such as those dictating how entire units can move or operate. 
Model Rules differentiate between the following cases (The same keywords also apply to Properties): 
 • Units entirely with X: whenever a Model Rule is referred to as units entirely with the rule, this refers to units where every single model in it has the Rule X or the Property X. 
 • Units containing X: whenever a Model Rule is referred to as units containing the rule, this refers to units where at least one model in it has the Rule X or the Property X. 
 • Units not containing X: whenever a Model Rule is referred to as units not containing the rule, this refers to units where no single model in it has the Rule X or the Property X.

sharedRules.name: Attack Attributes
sharedRules.description:
Attack Attributes is a subcategory of Model Rules. 
 While most Model Rules apply to the entire model (including all model parts on the same base), Attack Attributes are an exception, and only affect individual model parts, or even individual attacks. 
 Attack Attributes only affect Melee Attacks, unless otherwise stated. 
 There is one main exception to this: an Attack Attribute given specifically to a weapon, a spell or attack will affects it regardless of whether it would normally only be applicable to Melee Attacks. 
Attack Attributes are therefore written under the Offensive Characteristics part of a model entry, only affecting the specific model part they are listed under. 
 However, if an Attack Attribute is given to a unit (e.g. as a result of a spell), it applies to every model part in that unit; if given to a model, it applies to all parts of that model. 
 An Attack Attribute can also be given to a weapon, a spell, or an attack. Such Attack Attributes only affect attacks made with those specific sources. They will not affect other attacks made by the same model part (unless given specifically to another weapon, spell or attack by that model part).

sharedRules.name: Weapons
sharedRules.description:
Weapons is a subcategory of Model Rules. 
 Just as with Attack Attributes, a Weapon can only be used by the specific model part with the rule. 
 There are two types of weapons: 
 • Melee Weapon: a model part can only use a single Melee Weapon at a time, and only when Engaged in Combat. 
 If a model part is equipped with multiple Melee Weapons, the weapon it uses is determined in the First Round of Combat, with the following priority order: 
 • An Enchanted Weapon 
 • Any weapon that is neither a Hand Weapon, nor an Innate Weapon 
 • A Hand Weapon 
 • An Innate Weapon 
 This choice is then kept until the model is no longer Engaged in Combat. The effects of Melee Weapons only apply to the model part’s Standard Melee Attacks. 
 
 • If the Melee Weapon confers any modifier to Offensive Characteristics, as well as Attack Attributes, those effects are applied only to the model part’s Standard Melee Attacks. 
 • If the Melee Weapon confers any modifier to Global or Defensive Characteristics (Charge Speed, Mobility, Courage, Defensive Skill, Hit Points, Resilience, and Armour), as well as Model Rules that are not Attack Attributes, those effects are applied to the whole model (or model part, see rules for Character Mounts for details when and how the Characteristics of mounts are affected) at all times, except while using a different Melee Weapon. 
 • If the Melee Weapon confers any variable modifier (such as those based on a dice roll), the value of that modifier is determined at the start of the Agility Step in which the weapon is used. 
 
 
 • Shooting Weapons: Shooting Weapons are used for making Shooting Attacks. 
 Each model part can only use one Shooting Weapon per phase. 
 A Shooting Weapon generally has an Aim value, shown in brackets after the name of the weapon. The rules for each Shooting Weapon define its maximum Range, the number of Shots fired per attack, its attacks’ Strength and Armour Penetration, as well as any potential Attack Attributes applied to them.

sharedRules.name: Keywords
sharedRules.description:
Model Rules include keywords to help define their effects. 
 These keywords can be used directly within the Rulebook, and always apply to rules that have that keyword. 
 Alternatively, keywords can be specified for individual rules on specific models, spells, or weapons. In this case, this is indicated within brackets following the name of the rule. 
 List of Model Rule keywords: 
 • Cumulative: effects from multiple instances of a Model Rule with the Cumulative keyword are combined and add up. 
 • Distance Modifiers: written as a number followed by the " symbol. Any distance in the Model Rule description is replaced by that number. 
 For example, Vanguard (3 Mob) means that the model can perform a Vanguard move, but its Mobility is set to 3 instead of the normal 6. 
 • Shooting or Melee & Shooting: an Attack Attribute with the keyword Shooting only affects attacks that the model part makes with Shooting Weapons, while an Attack Attribute with the keyword Melee & Shooting affects both Melee Attacks and Shooting Attacks made by the model part. 
 • Remember that the default if none of these keywords are used is that Attack Attributes only affect Melee Attacks.
 For example, by default, Poison Attacks only affect Melee Attacks. However, if a model part has Poison Attacks (Shooting), this means the Poison Attacks Model Rule only applies to attacks made with that model part’s Shooting Weapons, unless it also has Poison Attacks or Poison Attacks (Melee & Shooting). 
 
 • Special Attacks: a model part with such a rule can make a special Melee Attack (which is not a Standard Melee Attack) that hits automatically.
 Since it is not a Standard Melee Attack, this attack can usually not be made as a Supporting Attack and does not suffer from Restricted Attacks (see the Melee Phase chapter).
 Special Attacks can be allocated onto any Attachable Model in units the attacker is Engaged in Combat with, if they are either or both: 
 Of a different Height than the Rank-and-File models in the unit.
In a unit with fewer than 5 Rank-and-File models (or fewer than 3 if they are of Height 3–5). 
 • Towards X: the Attack Attribute only applies if the attack is allocated to a specific type of enemy model or an enemy model that has certain rules or Properties. 
 The conditions are given as X. If more than one type of enemy is relevant, those types are separated by the word or. If multiple conditions must be fulfilled simultaneously, then they are separated by the word and.
 For example, Multiple Wounds (2, towards Height 4 and Beast, or Height 5) means that the rule Multiple Wounds is applied only when the attack is allocated either to a model that is both Height 4 and has the Property Beast, or to a model that is of Height 5, regardless of whether the model has the Property Beast. 
 • Against X: the Model Rule only applies when the model is attacked by a certain type of model or by a model or attack with certain rules or Properties. 
 For example, Hard Target (against Lethal Strike) means that the rule Hard Target applies only when the model is attacked by an attack with the Attribute Lethal Strike. See the rules under Towards X for how to interpret the words or and and. 
 • Unique Keywords: in addition to the standard Model Rule keywords defined above, certain Model Rules have unique keywords. These are defined in their respective rules.

If the model does not have Aegis, it instead gains Aegis (7 X+). For example, a model without Aegis that gains Aegis (+2) will gain Aegis (5+).

sharedRules.name: Ambush
sharedRules.description:
Any unit entirely with Ambush may choose to not be Deployed normally, but to be placed in Ambush by simply not being placed on the Battlefield during Deployment. A unit placed in Ambush will arrive on the Battlefield later during the game. 
 From your Player Turn 2 and onwards, roll a D6 for each unit placed in Ambush at the start of the Movement Phase: every unit that rolls a 3+ will arrive on the Battlefield if possible.
 During your Player Turn 5 and 6, this roll is always considered to have rolled a 3+.
 When a unit arrives on the Battlefield, choose a point as specified by X. If no suitable point is available where the unit can be placed on the Battlefield, the unit cannot arrive on the Battlefield this turn.
 
 Deploy each unit arriving on the Battlefield with at least three of its four corners within 6" from the chosen point in any valid formation following the Unit Spacing rule.
 There must be no other units or Impassable Terrain directly located between any point on the Unit Boundary and the chosen point. See the figure below for examples.
 Ambushing units count as having performed an Advance Move when they arrive on the Battlefield, and cannot perform any Move in the same Phase. 
 If an Ambushing unit does not arrive on the Battlefield by the end of the game, it is removed as a casualty.
 An Attachable Model placed in Ambush can be Deployed joined to a unit placed in Ambush with the same X value, following the usual restrictions. It may choose a unit to be joined to during each of your Player Turns, before rolling to see if your Ambushing units arrive on the Battlefield. 
 Make a single dice roll for the Combined Unit. 
 Note: Attached has no effect on this; the choice of a unit to be Deployed in Ambush in may change each turn.
 
 A unit arriving on the Battlefield in Game Turn 6 loses Scoring. 
 
 Deploying Ambushing units.In these examples, the unit has Ambush (Battlefield Edge). The unit with the yellow check mark is placed in a valid position, while the two units with red crosses are not: the left one because there is an Impassable Terrain Feature between the Unit Boundary and the chosen point, and the right one because parts of the unit are more than 6" away from the chosen point.

 • If a unit has multiple instances of Exclusive, all criteria must be fulfilled together. 
 The specific criteria for X can be unit names, Model Rules, Properties, upgrades, etc. 
 If a model has both Exclusive and Attached, apply all requirements from both rules (remember that a model that cannot be Deployed is considered a casualty).

sharedRules.name: Feigned Flight
sharedRules.description:
A unit entirely with Feigned Flight automatically passes any Rally Test it takes after voluntarily becoming Shaken. 
 In addition, models with Fearless and Feigned Flight ignore Fearless for the purposes of choosing 'Flee!' as a Charge reaction. I.e. if every model with Fearless in a (combined) unit has Feigned Flight, the unit can 'Flee!'.

sharedRules.name: Fly
sharedRules.description:
Units entirely with Fly ignore Terrain Features, Open Terrain and other units during Move Manoeuvres and Charge Moves. 
 The unit must follow the Unit Spacing rule at the end of any of its moves, and Terrain Features and Open Terrain from which the model starts or ends its move still affect it. 
 The charged unit is not ignored during a Charge Move, and there must be room for the unit’s Front Facing to be placed in contact with the charged unit before the initial Align Move.

sharedRules.name: Frenzy
sharedRules.description: Units containing Frenzy must always choose to Pursue (including Overrun) when able to.

sharedRules.name: General
sharedRules.description:
An army may include a General.

This upgrade is Legendary.

The General gains Commanding Presence (see Model Rules).

sharedRules.name: Ghost Step
sharedRules.description:
A unit entirely with Ghost Step ignores Terrain Features and Open Terrain when moving. 
 The unit must follow the Unit Spacing rule at the end of its move.
 A Health Pool with Ghost Step never fulfils the criteria for which models must take Dangerous Terrain Tests due to Terrain Features (but still needs to take Dangerous Terrain Tests from other sources than Terrain Features, such as when making a Flee Move through an enemy unit). 
 If the unit ends a move inside Impassable Terrain, backtrack the move to the unit’s last valid position, unless as part of a Flee Move, in which case the standard Flee Moves rules apply.

sharedRules.name: Hard Target
sharedRules.description: Shooting Attacks allocated against a Health Pool with Hard Target suffer -X to hit.

sharedRules.name: Hidden
sharedRules.description:
The model is not Deployed as normal.
 Instead, at the start of any Player Turn, it may choose a friendly Rank-and-File model, which satisfy the following criteria: 
 • The model with Hidden could normally have joined the unit. 
 • The model with Hidden has an identical base size and Height as the Rank-and-File models in the unit. 
 • The unit is not Shaken and is not a Summoned unit but it can be Engaged in Combat. 
 After choosing an eligible unit, follow these steps: 
 • Remove a Rank-and-File model, with the same base size as the model with Hidden, from the front rank of the chosen unit as a casualty. 
 • Deploy the model with Hidden where the removed model was positioned. 
 If the chosen unit is engaged in Combat when being joined by a model with Hidden, consider the model with Hidden to be in First Round of Combat for all rules purposes, with Duration: End of Turn. 
Note: Attachable models with Hidden can still be Deployed using the Hidden rules.

sharedRules.name: Hit and Run
sharedRules.description:
A unit entirely with Hit and Run in contact with an enemy unit may choose to voluntarily become “Broken” at the start of Take Break Tests (step 4.C of a Round of Combat). In that case, the unit is considered to have failed a Break Test and is ignored for the rest of step 4.C. 
 If the unit was on the winning side of the Round of Combat, the enemy cannot Pursue. 
 Note: this means units with Supernal, Unstable suffer no Health Point loss if they voluntarily become “Broken”.

sharedRules.name: Horror
sharedRules.description:
Flee Moves from enemy units made in the following situations gain two instances of Minimised: 
 • Flee! Charge Reactions declared when Charged by a unit containing Horror (Flee! Charge Reactions declared when later Charged by other units are unaffected). 
 • Breaking from Combat while in contact with one or more units containing Horror. 
 Remember that units containing Fearless are unaffected by this rule.

sharedRules.name: Immune
sharedRules.description: Attacks with the Attack Attributes or Properties stated in brackets (X) allocated against a model with Immune (X) lose those Attack Attributes or Properties.

sharedRules.name: Insignificant
sharedRules.description: Units entirely with Insignificant do not cause Panic Tests on units not containing Insignificant when making Flee Moves through them.

sharedRules.name: Beacon of Courage
sharedRules.description:
Friendly models in units within X" of a non- Shaken friendly model with Beacon of Courage benefit from Courageous.
 Courageous: a unit containing Courageous must reroll failed Courage Tests.

sharedRules.name: Light Troops
sharedRules.description:
A unit entirely with Light Troops can perform Reform Move Manoeuvres up to twice its Mobility (instead of the normal half Mobility).
 If, while doing a Reform Move Manoeuvre, its centre moves further than its Mobility, the move is considered a March Move for the purpose of rules triggered due to Marching (e.g. Dangerous Terrain Test and, if Undead, being restricted from performing a March Move, etc.).
 For the purpose of shooting, this is still a Reform Move. I.e. the unit can shoot if moving further than its Mobility
 Note: this rule has no effect on other Move Manoeuvres, including March Moves A unit containing Light Troops is always considered to have zero Proper Ranks; ignore Attachable Models with Light Troops joined to a unit for this purpose, unless the unit consists of only Attachable Models.

sharedRules.name: Magic Resistance
sharedRules.description:
Whenever an enemy spell targets one or more friendly units containing Magic Resistance: 
 • Identify the highest Magic Resistance value across all targeted friendly units 
 • Reduce the Casting Roll by this value

sharedRules.name: Mindless
sharedRules.description: A unit entirely with this rule automatically passes its Command Tests for Combat Reform, and automatically fails its Command Tests for Redirecting Charges.

sharedRules.name: Musician
sharedRules.description:
Musician is a unit-wide upgrade, normally represented by the presence of a regimental musician.
 When performing a Reform Move or a Combat Reform, a unit containing a Musician may change the number of its files by 5 rather than the normal 1. 
 In addition, units containing Musician benefit from a +1 Discipline modifier when taking Command Tests.

sharedRules.name: Parry
sharedRules.description:
Against Melee Attacks made by an attacker Engaged in the models Front Facing, the Defensive Skill of a model with Parry is always at least equal to the Offensive Skill of the attacker.
 Remember that since Parry provides a modifier to a Defensive Characteristic, its effects do not apply to a Character on a mount that has its own Defensive Skill.

sharedRules.name: Random Movement
sharedRules.description:
Units entirely with Random Movement do not follow normal rules for Charging, Move Manoeuvres, Pursue Moves or Flee Moves. 
 Instead, apply the following: 
 • During the Charge Phase, the unit cannot Declare any Charges. 
 • At any time the unit would perform a Move Manoeuvre, it performs a Pursue Move instead (see the Melee Phase chapter), with the following exceptions: 
 • It must move in the Movement Phase if allowed to do so, and it must do so before any units without Random Movement have performed their Move Manoeuvres. 
 • It moves the distance stated in brackets (X). 
 • It can choose in which direction it will move (the owning player must choose the direction before rolling the Pursuit Distance). 
 • It does not take Dangerous Terrain Tests, unless Charging. 
 • It treats the Battlefield Edge as Impassable Terrain. 
 • That move counts as an Advance Move for the purpose of Moving and Shooting. 
 
 • The unit’s Pursue and Flee Moves use the distance stated in brackets (X) instead of the normal distance. 
 • The unit cannot perform any Magical Move nor use Vanguard. 
 Whenever a rule requires the Mobility or Charge Speed of a model with this rule, use the potential maximum value of X (eg. if X is 2D6", then consider the Mobility and Charge Speed to be equal to 12"). 
 It also means that effects that modify its Pursue Distance, such as Maximised and Minimised, also affect its moves.

sharedRules.name: Regeneration
sharedRules.description:
Regeneration is a Special Save, with a value indicated in brackets (X). 
 If X is given as a modifier and with a maximum value (e.g. +2), the model gains this as a modifier to all its Regeneration Special Save rolls, which can never be increased to rolls better than 3+. If the model does not have Regeneration, it instead gains Regeneration (7 X+). For example, a model without Regeneration that gains Regeneration (+2) will gain Regeneration (5+).
 
 Note that Regeneration Saves cannot be taken against attacks with Flaming Attacks, nor against attacks with Lethal Strike that roll a ‘6’ to wound.

sharedRules.name: Resistance
sharedRules.description:
Attacks allocated against the model’s Health Pool must reroll successful to-wound rolls.
 If Resistance is associated with an Attack Attribute, Property or Rule in brackets (X), then it only applies against attacks with that Attack Attribute or made by a model with that Property or Rule.

sharedRules.name: Resolute
sharedRules.description:
A unit containing Resolute and that has at least one Proper Rank is considered to have one additional Proper Rank when Engaged in Combat. 
Note: this is applied before applying the effects of Surrounded.

sharedRules.name: Scout
sharedRules.description:
Units entirely with Scout are not required to be Deployed inside their Deployment Zone: instead, they can be Deployed anywhere on the Battlefield, at least 12" away from the opponent’s Deployment Zone.
 A unit that starts the game outside its own Deployment Zone cannot declare a Charge in the first Player Turn of the first Game Turn.

sharedRules.name: Shield
sharedRules.description:
A model with Shield is considered to be using a Shield at all times, except during the Melee Phase if it is using a Two-Handed Melee Weapon. 
 A model using a Shield gains +1 Arm. 
 In addition, any Height 1-3 model using a Hand Weapon while using a Shield gains Parry.
 Note: Shield provides no benefit against Melee Attacks when using a Two-Handed Melee Weapon .
 Remember that since Shield (and parry) provide modifiers to Defensive Characteristics, their effects do not apply to a Character on a mount that has its own Defensive Skill or Armour.

sharedRules.name: Skirmisher
sharedRules.description:
Units containing Skirmisher adopt a unique formation, called a Skirmish Formation. Instead of being in contact with each other, these models are placed 12.5mm apart from each other (roughly half an inch, see the figure below). 
 These gaps between the models are considered part of the unit for Cover and Line of Sight purposes, and have the same Height as the unit. 
 Other than this gap between models, units with Skirmisher follow the normal rules for forming units and therefore have a Front, two Flanks, and a Rear Facing, can perform Supporting Attacks, and so on.
 Units in Skirmish Formation can only be joined by Attachable Models that have the same Height as the unit. 
 Unless an Attachable Model has the exact same base size as all Rank-and-File models in the unit, it is considered Mismatched for the purpose of placement within the unit. 
 The unit ceases to be in Skirmish Formation when all models with Skirmisher have been removed. When this happens, contract their Skirmish Formation into a normal formation when returning the unit into a valid formation, without moving the centre of the first rank. If Engaged in Combat, nudge any unit as normal to maintain contact. 
 
See figure figure/skirmisher for an illustration of this rule. 
 Skirmish formation.An example of a unit in Skirmish Formation with a joined Mismatching Character. All models are 12.5 mm away from each other.\ The same unit Engaged in Combat. Only darkened models may attack. Models with a dashed frame can attack a Character (either C1 or C2). Models with a lighter shade cannot attack at all.

sharedRules.name: Solitary
sharedRules.description: Units containing Solitary can never join other units, and can never be joined by other models.

sharedRules.name: Standard Bearer
sharedRules.description:
Standard Bearer is a unit-wide upgrade, normally represented by the presence of a model carrying the unit standard, icon, military insignia, totem, or other similar symbol. 
 A unit containing a Standard Bearer adds +1 to the Combat Score of its side.

sharedRules.name: Stand Behind
sharedRules.description:
Attachable Models with Stand Behind are not required to have their Front Facing as far forward as possible within their unit this generally means that the model can be positioned anywhere within its unit. 
 This rule cannot be used while the model has a Mismatching base to its unit.

sharedRules.name: Strider
sharedRules.description:
If Strider is associated with a specific type of Terrain, which would be indicated in brackets (X). In such cases, Strider only affects the unit’s interaction with this Terrain Feature. 
 Models with Strider may ignore rules associated with Terrain Features, with the following exceptions: 
 • They cannot ignore any rule affecting Line of Sight or Cover. 
 • They cannot ignore any rule associated with Weakness. 
 • They cannot ignore the Impassable rule of Impassable Terrain. 
 A Health Pool with Strider never fulfils the criteria for which models must take Dangerous Terrain Tests due to the associated Terrain Feature (but still needs to take Dangerous Terrain Tests from other sources, such as Terrain Features not associated with its Strider rule, or when making a Flee Move through an enemy unit). 
 In addition, if the unit contains a Rank-and-File model with Strider, it ignores the Disruptive rule of any Terrain Feature associated to its Strider rule.

sharedRules.name: Stubborn
sharedRules.description:
When a unit containing Stubborn loses a Round of Combat, halve the penalty to its Discipline from the Combat Score difference, rounding fractions up (i.e. towards a larger modifier). 
 If the unit is also Steady, the modifier is first set to no smaller than -2 (following the Steady rules), and then halved, rounding up, to -1.
 If the unit is Unstable, the Health Point losses due to Unstable are halved, rounding fractions up (i.e. towards more Health Point losses).

sharedRules.name: Supernal
sharedRules.description:
When a unit entirely with Supernal fails a Break Test, instead of being Broken and subsequently Shaken, it suffers a number of Health Point losses equal to the amount by which the combat was lost (with no saves of any kind allowed). These Health Point losses are first allocated towards Rank-and-File models, and once enough Health Points losses are suffered to remove all Rank-and-File models, any remaining Health Point losses are allocated by the owner towards Attachable Models, as evenly as possible. 
Attachable Models with Supernal can only join units containing Supernal, and units containing Supernal can only be joined by Attachable Models with Supernal.

sharedRules.name: Swiftstride
sharedRules.description: Rolls for Charge Range, Flee Distance and Pursue Distance by units entirely with Swiftstride gain Maximised.

sharedRules.name: Terror
sharedRules.description:
When a unit containing Terror declares a Charge in the Charge Phase, the target must take a Panic Test. If the test is failed, the unit must choose Flee! as its Charge Reaction if allowed to do so (e.g. not already Engaged in Combat, etc.).
 Note that this Flee Move is not voluntary: friendly units may therefore be required to take a Panic Test when moving through them. 
 Units containing Terror are themselves immune to the effects of Terror.

sharedRules.name: Undead
sharedRules.description:
Units containing Undead can perform March Moves only if they benefit from a friendly model’s Commanding Presence. For this purpose, any Reform Move exceeding a unit’s Mobility count as a March Move.
 Moreover, models with Undead have an additional characteristic called Resurrect (Rsr) on their statline, which can interact with some other game effects.

sharedRules.name: Unruly
sharedRules.description: Command Tests taken by a unit containing this rule gain Maximised.

sharedRules.name: Unstable
sharedRules.description:
Whenever a unit entirely with Unstable would take a Break Test, it suffers instead a number of Health Point losses equal to the amount by which the Combat was lost (with no saves of any kind allowed). These Health Point losses are first allocated towards Rank-and-File models, and once enough Health Points losses are suffered to remove all Rank-and-File models, any remaining Health Point losses are allocated by the owner towards Attachable Models, as evenly as possible. 
Those Health Point losses can be reduced in the following ways: 
 • If the unit contains Stubborn, the Health Point losses are halved, rounding fractions up. 
 • If the unit is affected by Beacon of Courage, the Health Point losses are reduced by 1. 
 • If the unit is Steady while affected by Beacon of Courage, the Health Point losses are reduced by an additional 1. 
 • If the unit is Solid while affected by Beacon of Courage, the Health Point losses are reduced by an additional 1. 
 I.e. a unit that is affected by Beacon of Courage while also being Steadfast reduces its Health Point losses by a total of 3. Attachable Models with Unstable can only join units containing Unstable, and units containing Unstable can only be joined by Attachable Models with Unstable.

sharedRules.name: Vanguard
sharedRules.description:
After Deployment, units entirely with Vanguard may perform a pre-game Reform, Advance, or March Move, called a Vanguard Move, with the following exceptions: 
 • If a value X is given, the units Mobility is always X during the Vanguard Move otherwise use the units Mobility. 
 • No model can move further than 12" during the Vanguard Move, regardless of its Mobility. 
 • The unit cannot end the Vanguard Move within 6" of an enemy unit. 
 • Attachable Models cannot leave a unit as part of the Vanguard Move. 
 If both players have units entirely with Vanguard, they alternate moving their units one by one, starting with the unit the Defender has given Vanguard (3 Mob) to.
 A unit that starts the game outside its own Deployment Zone cannot declare a Charge in the first Player Turn of the first Game Turn.

sharedRules.name: War Platform
sharedRules.description:
The model follows the rules for Attachable Models, with the following exceptions: 
 • It can never perform Make Way moves (not even if it is also a Character). 
 • Ranged Attacks allocated onto a unit with a War Platform joined to it can only target the War Platform if there are fewer than 5 Rank-and-File models (or fewer than 3 if they are of Height 3–5) in the unit.(if there are no Rank-and-File models in the unit, ignore this rule) 
 • Any given unit can never contain more than a single model with War Platform at a time. 
 When the model is joined to a unit, its Mobility and Charge Speed is set to that of its unit, with the following exceptions: 
 • If there are no Rank-and-File models from the unit in contact with the War Platform’s flank Facings (right and left side), the model must use its own Mobility and Charge Speed instead. Meaning that, if slower than the unit, the unit’s Mobility and Charge Speed are set to those of the War Platform. 
 • The War Platform cannot use the unit’s Mobility and Charge Speed values when leaving the unit (including Charging out of it). Instead, it uses its own Mobility and Charge Speed.

sharedRules.name: Weakness
sharedRules.description:
Attacks allocated against the model’s Health Pool must reroll failed to-wound rolls.
 If Weakness is associated with an Attack Attribute, Property or Rule, which would be indicated in brackets (X), it only applies against attacks with the indicated Attack Attribute or made by a model with the indicated Property or Rule.

sharedRules.name: Wizard Adept
sharedRules.description:
The model becomes a Wizard, gains Channel (1), and knows 3 different Learned Spells, chosen from the Apprentice Spell and the Adept Spells ( #1 – #4) of the Magic Path it has chosen. 
 It may Swap Spells during Pre-game Selections. See the Battle Preparation chapter for details.

sharedRules.name: Wizard Apprentice
sharedRules.description:
The model becomes a Wizard, knows 1 Learned Spell, which is the Apprentice Spell ( #1) of the Path it has chosen. 
 It may Swap Spells during Pre-game Selections. See the Battle Preparation chapter for details.

sharedRules.name: Wizard Conclave
sharedRules.description:
The unit knows X different Learned Spells, chosen from the list of available spells in its unit entry, is a Wizard and, if X is 2 or more, it also gains Channel (1). 
 The unit may only do a Hereditary Swap if it could have picked the Hereditary Spell during Spell Selection (as part of Pre-game Planning), however it is still eligible for a Universal Swap. See Battle Preparation chapter for details. 
 Even though the spells are known to the whole unit, only one model is a Caster: every time you cast the spell, just before choosing the targets, select one Rank-and-File model as the Caster for this spell. 
 If a Wizard Conclave suffers a Miscast, treat the entire unit as the Caster. 
 For the purpose of Primary and Secondary Objectives treat the entire unit as a Caster.

sharedRules.name: Wizard Master
sharedRules.description:
Wizard Master only
The model becomes a Wizard, gains Channel (2) and knows 5 different Learned Spells, chosen from the Apprentice Spell, the Adept, and Master Spells ( #1 – #6) of the Magic Path it has chosen. 
 It may Swap Spells during Pre-game Selections. See the Battle Preparation chapter for details.

sharedRules.name: Accurate
sharedRules.description: An attack with Accurate does not suffer the -1 to-hit modifier for shooting at Long Range.

sharedRules.name: Area Attack
sharedRules.description:
Before making a Shooting Attack with Area Attack, determine the attack’s Target Facing using the same rules as for Cover. 
 • If the attack hits in the Front or Rear: select up to Y different ranks of the target. 
 • If the attack hits in the Flank: select up to Y different files of the target. 
 For each rank or file chosen this way, the unit takes X hits, up to a maximum equal to the number of models in that rank or file.
 An Area Attack can not cause more hits than the total models in the unit, and no single model can suffer more than one hit from each Area Attack. 
 Remember that attacks multiplied into several hits are allocated after establishing how many hits are scored (i.e. after the attack has hit).
 Figure figure/areaattack illustrates different variations of Area Attack. 
 Examples of Area Attacks. Units A to D are hit by an Area Attack (33) that has their Front as its Target Facing.\ A: There are 3 ranks with more than 3 models. Number of hits: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.\ B: The first rank has more than 3 models, but the second rank only has 2 models. There is no third rank. Number of hits: 3 + 2 = 5.\ C: Since there is only a single model, there will always only be a single rank with a single model. Number of hits: 1.\ D: The first and second rank have 3 models. There is no third rank. Number of hits: 3 + 3 = 6.\\ Units E and F are hit by an Area Attack (14).\ E: The attack has the Front of the unit as its Target Facing. The first and second rank have more than 1 model. There is no third or fourth rank. Number of hits: 1 + 1 = 2.\ F: The attack has the Flank of the unit as its Target Facing. There are more than 4 files with 1 or more models. Number of hits: 1 + 1 +1 +1 = 4.

sharedRules.name: Artillery
sharedRules.description:
An attack with Artillery ignores to-hit modifiers from Cover. 
 In addition, it gains +1 to-hit when shooting at units that are Solid, have Height 5, or both.

sharedRules.name: Automatic Hits
sharedRules.description:
An attack with Automatic Hits does not roll to hit, but always hits automatically.
 This rule is shortened to Auto when used as a weapon’s Aim.

sharedRules.name: Crush Attack
sharedRules.description: When a model part with Crush Attack allocates its attacks in Combat, it may choose to exchange all of its Standard Melee Attacks for a single Standard Melee Attack, which has its Strength and Armour Penetration both set to 10 and gains Multiple Wounds (D3). This cannot be done as a Restricted Attack.

sharedRules.name: Devastating Charge
sharedRules.description:
A Charging model part with Devastating Charge, or using a weapon with Devastating Charge, gains the Rules and Characteristic modifiers stated in brackets. 
 For example, a model part with Devastating Charge (+1 Str) gains +1 Str when Charging.

sharedRules.name: Direct Hit
sharedRules.description:
When an attack with Direct Hit hits, after determining the number of hits (e.g. in the case of Area Attack), a single hit, chosen by the attacker, gains the Rules and Characteristic modifiers stated in brackets. 
 If a Strength and/or Armour Penetration is given directly, set the attack’s Strength and/or Armour Penetration to that value (for example, Direct Hit (Str 10, AP 6) means one hit from that attack has its Strength set to 10 and its Armour Penetration set to 6
.

sharedRules.name: Divine Attacks
sharedRules.description: Aegis Saves cannot be taken against Divine Attacks.

sharedRules.name: Elven Finesse
sharedRules.description: A model part with this Attack Attribute attacking with a Great Weapon strikes at -1 Agility instead of always at Agility 0.

sharedRules.name: Extra Support
sharedRules.description: A model part with Extra Support replaces the limit on the maximum number of attacks the model can do as Restricted Attacks with the value in brackets (X) or, if it includes a +, increases that limit with +X.

sharedRules.name: Fight in Extra Rank
sharedRules.description: A model part with Fight in Extra Rank, or using a weapon with Fight in Extra Rank, can make Supporting Attacks from one additional rank.

sharedRules.name: First Strike
sharedRules.description:
During its First Round of Combat, any model part with First Strike, or using a weapon with First Strike, gains the Rules and Characteristic modifiers stated in brackets. 
 For example, a model part with First Strike (+1 Str) gains +1 Str in its First Round of Combat.

sharedRules.name: Flaming Attacks
sharedRules.description: Regeneration Saves cannot be taken against Flaming Attacks.

sharedRules.name: Fury
sharedRules.description: If the attack hits with a to-hit roll of ‘6’, it causes one additional hit (usually this means it causes two hits instead of one). This additional hit is allocated towards the same target.

sharedRules.name: Grind Attack
sharedRules.description:
A model part with a Grind Attack can make a Special Attack which is resolved at the model part’s Agility, and inflicts X hits, using the model part’s Strength, Armour Penetration, and Attack Attributes, but not Weapons. 
 Remember that attacks multiplied into several hits are allocated after establishing how many hits are scored (i.e. after the attack has hit).

sharedRules.name: Hand-and-a-Half
sharedRules.description: The model part ignores Two-Handed, and its weapons count as a Hand Weapon for the purpose of Shield (while keeping other rules and modifiers).

sharedRules.name: Hatred
sharedRules.description: An attack with Hatred must reroll failed to-hit rolls.

sharedRules.name: Impact Hits
sharedRules.description:
If Charging, the model part can make a Special Attack which is resolved at Agility Step 10, and inflicts X hits, using the model part’s Strength, Armour Penetration, and Attack Attributes, but not Weapons. 
 Remember that attacks multiplied into several hits are allocated after establishing how many hits are scored (i.e. after the attack has hit). If more than one model part of a combined model has Impact Hits, only a single model part (chosen by the model’s owner) can perform its Impact Hits in a Round of Combat.

sharedRules.name: Lethal Strike
sharedRules.description: If an attack with Lethal Strike wounds with a to-wound roll of ‘6’, its Armour Penetration is always 10, and Regeneration Saves cannot be taken against it.

sharedRules.name: Lightning Attacks
sharedRules.description: Lightning Attacks must reroll failed to-wound rolls towards models without Metal Armour.

sharedRules.name: Magical Attacks
sharedRules.description: This Attack Attribute does not confer any direct effects, but instead interacts with other rules, such as Aegis (X, against Magical Attacks).

sharedRules.name: March and Shoot
sharedRules.description: Performing a March Move in the same Player Turn does not prevent shooting with attacks or model parts that have March and Shoot. (The the attack can still suffer -1 to hit for Moving and Shooting).

sharedRules.name: Multiple Wounds
sharedRules.description:
Health Point losses caused by the attack are multiplied into the value given in brackets (X). If the value is a dice, roll one dice for each unsaved wound from an attack with Multiple Wounds. 
 The number of Health Point losses that the attack is multiplied into can never be higher than the Health Points Characteristic of the target (excluding Health Points lost previously in the battle).
 For example, if an attack with Multiple Wounds (D6) wounds a unit of Trolls (HP 3) and rolls a ‘5’ for the multiplier, the number of Health Points lost is reduced to 3, even if the Troll unit has already lost one or two Health Points previously in battle.

sharedRules.name: Poison Attacks
sharedRules.description:
Whenever an attack with Poison Attacks hits with a to-hit roll of ‘6’, it wounds automatically (no to-wound roll needed). 
 If the attack has two or more instances of Poison Attacks, it wounds automatically on a successful to-hit roll of ‘5’ or ‘6’ instead. 
 If the attack is turned into more than one hit (e.g. a hit with Area Attack, Fury), only a single hit, chosen by the attacker, wounds automatically. All other hits must roll to wound as normal.

sharedRules.name: Press of Ranks
sharedRules.description: An attack with Press of Ranks gains +1 to wound, to a maximum of 3+.

sharedRules.name: Psychic Attacks
sharedRules.description: When rolling to wound with a Psychic Attack, replace the target’s Resilience with its Discipline.

sharedRules.name: Quick to Fire
sharedRules.description: An attack with Quick to Fire does not suffer the -1 to-hit modifier for Moving and Shooting.

sharedRules.name: Rage
sharedRules.description:
Whenever the model loses a Health Point, it gains +1 Att. 
 Whenever it Recovers or Raises a Health Point, it suffers -1 Att

sharedRules.name: Shoot in Extra Rank
sharedRules.description:
A model part with Shoot in Extra Rank may use Shooting Attacks from one additional rank. 
 Normally, this means that it will be able to make Shooting Attacks from the third rank.

sharedRules.name: Stand and Shoot
sharedRules.description:
A model part with Stand and Shoot may perform an out of sequence Shooting Attack, when an enemy unit successfully performs a Charge Move that brings it in contact with the model part’s unit, if the following conditions are met: 
 • The model part’s unit is not Engaged in Combat with any other units. 
 Note: this means that during a Combined Charge, only the first Charging Unit moved can be targeted, except if the Charging Unit is removed at the end of its move. As long as the Charging Unit is removed at the end of its move, there is no limit on the amount of times a unit can Stand and Shoot. 
 
 • The enemy unit Charges the model part’s unit in its Front Facing. 
 • The enemy unit started the Charge further away than its Charge Speed (using the lowest Charge Speed in the unit 
 • The Charge was not done as part of a Pursue Move. 
 
 This is a Shooting Attack that does not require Line of Sight, can be done even if the enemy unit is not in the shooter’s Front Arc, and is always resolved against the target unit’s (i.e., the Charging unit’s) Front Facing.

sharedRules.name: Stomp Attack
sharedRules.description: A model part with Stomp Attack can make a Special Attack which is resolved at Agility Step 0, can only be allocated towards a Health Pool of Height 0–1, and inflicts X hits, using the model part’s Strength, Armour Penetration and Attack Attributes, but not Weapons. If more than one model part of a combined model has Stomp Attack, only a single model part (chosen by the model’s owner) can perform its Stomp Attack in each Round of Combat.

sharedRules.name: Sweeping Attack
sharedRules.description:
When a model with Sweeping Attack is within 1" of an Unengaged enemy unit during a Move Manoeuvre (even temporarily), the model’s unit may perform a Sweeping Attack against that enemy unit. This can only be used once per friendly Player Turn. 
 Resolve the Sweeping Attack when the Move Manoeuvre is completed. The attack hits automatically, and counts as a Ranged Attack.
